title: Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. & Scarpella et al. (2006) Genes Dev. — PIN1 Efflux Carrier Allocation, Intracellular Pool Conservation, and Open Dendritic Trees vs Closed Reticulate Venation Loops on Hexagonal Leaf Lamina Lattices
organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (dicot leaf lamina and procambial venation network)

primary_sources.citation: Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. 236(4):366-375 (PMID 15899502; Pass 3 corrected from the erroneous 236(3):313-325)
primary_sources.role: Coupled ODEs for intracellular auxin S_i and directional PIN1 efflux carriers P_ij on a 2D hexagonal leaf lamina lattice: dS_i/dt = sigma - mu*S_i - sum_j J_{i->j}, J_{i->j} = P_ij*S_i - P_ji*S_j + D*(S_i - S_j), and dP_ij/dt = k_1*Phi(J_{i->j})*P_{i,cyt} - k_2*P_ij with conserved total cellular carrier pool P_total = P_{i,cyt} + sum_{j=1}^6 P_ij. Demonstrates that conserved linear/power-law allocation Phi(J) = max(0,J)^p (p > 1) drives winner-take-all single-face polarization and strictly open hierarchical dendritic trees (Betti-1 = 0), whereas nonlinear saturating allocation Phi(J) = J^n / (K^n + J^n) allows multi-face co-polarization and closed reticulate venation loops (Betti-1 > 0)

primary_sources.citation: Scarpella, Marcos, Friml & Berleth (2006) Genes & Development 20(8):1015-1027
primary_sources.role: Live imaging of ProPIN1:PIN1-GFP in developing Arabidopsis thaliana leaves showing that epidermal PIN1 convergence points initiate secondary veins and that transient bipolar (double-headed) PIN1 cells bridge nascent secondary strands to preexisting primary/secondary veins to close areole loops
Theoretical and computational analysis of open vs closed venation loop formation in Arabidopsis leaves under carrier-driven canalization, moving auxin sources, and bipolar cell bridging

primary_sources.citation: Stoma, Lucas, Chopard, Schaedel, Traas & Godin (2008) PLoS Comput. Biol. 4(10):e1000207
primary_sources.role: Flux-based PIN1 carrier allocation and conservation of intracellular + membrane PIN pools during canalized auxin transport

model_a_open_tree.description: Feugier et al. (2005) Model A: conserved intracellular PIN1 pool with non-saturating quadratic flux allocation Phi(J) = J^2

model_b_saturating_reticulate.description: Feugier et al. (2005) Model B & Scarpella et al. (2006): saturating Hill exocytosis Phi(J) = J^2/(K^2+J^2) + marginal epidermal PIN1 convergence points

pin1_exocytosis_ablation_control.description: Negative control: k_1 = 0 (gnom / brefeldin-A PIN1 exocytosis block or pin1 null mutant)
